title: Offline bundle curation and install manifest
content: Purpose: This doc is a pragmatic playbook for curating, transporting, installing, and upgrading Redwood Private in fully air-gapped or heavily restricted VPCs. It focuses on the end-to-end artifact bundle lifecycle (collection, signing, verification, transport, seed/restore, upgrade), plus notes for Terraform module variables and validation checks. Aim: give SRE/SE or customer ops a single manifest to run through and a repeatable checklist for installs and upgrades. Scope and assumptions: - Target: on-prem / sealed VPC installs where outbound access is blocked. - Cluster type: Kubernetes (RKE/AKS/EKS-distroless not assumed) with control-plane accessible to operator-runner. - OS: Ubuntu/CentOS variants supported. - Transport media: secure scp over temporary bastion, removable drives, or pre-provisioned internal HTTP server. - This is not the complete install guide — it complements the operator docs and the airgap runtime repo. Roles and responsibilities (recommended): - Customer infra / partner: provides physical media or secure transfer channel and local registry. - Redwood private-deploy team: produces curated bundle artifact and verification signatures, provides terraform variable set and migration scripts. - Onsite SRE: performs import, runs preflight, shares verification hashes. High-level flow: 1) Generate bundle manifest and artifact list on online staging environment. 2) Sign artifacts and manifest (cosign/GPG). 3) Transfer bundle to customer-controlled transport medium. 4) Seed local registry (Harbor/registry:2) and package mirrors (apt/yum/pip). 5) Run preflight checks and apply Terraform with offline vars. 6) Deploy operator and run post-install validation. 7) For upgrades: staged rollout, smoke tests, rollback plan. Artifact bundle composition (recommended minimal contents): - metadata/manifest.yaml (see manifest format example below) - container-images.tar.gz (docker save of all images + repo mapping CSV) - helm-charts.tgz (all charts required, operator chart included) - control-plane-binaries.tar.gz (redwoodctl, bootstrap scripts) - operator-bundle/ (OCS operator bundle or operator manifest directory) - database-migrations.sql.gz (if stateful components need migration) - os-packages/ (apt repo snapshot or yum repo rpms) - python-wheels/ (wheelhouse for runtime and eval tooling) - model-weights/ (if customer is shipping models; ensure separate consent/size note) - signatures/ (cosign sigs, GPG sigs for manifest and critical binaries) - checksums.txt (sha256/sha512 for all top-level artifacts) Manifest format (simple YAML we publish alongside bundle): - bundle_version: string - created_by: name/email - created_at: YYYY-MM-DD - artifacts: list of {name, path, sha256, size_bytes, type (image/chart/package)} - registry_map: list of {original_repo, mirrored_repo} - terraform_module_version: git@...#tag or module checksum - required_k8s_version: semver - known_issues: free text Signing & verification guidance: - Use cosign to sign OCI images (preferred): cosign sign --key cosign.key - For tarballs and executables, use GPG detached signatures: gpg --output file.sig --detach-sig file.tgz - Provide a signed manifest and a top-level bundle.sig (GPG) so the onsite team can verify everything before import. - Include a small verification script verify-bundle.sh that: - checks checksums.txt, - verifies GPG signatures against a provided fingerprint, - validates cosign signed images by attempting a local registry push dry-run or using cosign verify. Registry seeding strategies (pick one): A) Registry import (preferred): - Start local registry (harbor or registry:2) inside customer network. - Use skopeo or docker load: load images from container-images.tar.gz and tag/push to local registry as per registry_map. - Verify images by pulling them back to a test node. B) Registry proxy + pull-through: - For customers with partial egress, preseed a proxy that can pull from a temporary bastion and cache images. C) File-based: - For fully isolated envs, use docker load on nodes and retag images to local registry naming, then push to registry installed in-cluster. Notes: keep registry_map consistent with Terraform variables so the platform knows where to pull images during boot. Package mirrors (apt/yum/pip): - For apt: use reprepro to create a snapshot repo. Provide Release files and signed InRelease. - For yum: create a cerated repo dir with repodata; serve via local HTTP. - For pip: wheelhouse + simple index (static HTML) or devpi server archive. - Terraform modules that usually download remote providers should be baked into the bundle (mirror provider plugins or use local provider plugins). Terraform module notes (variables & patterns to ensure offline installs): - var.offline_registry (string) => host:port to seed images - var.offline_chart_repo (string) => URL of local helm repo - var.bundle_version (string) => aligns with manifest.bundle_version - var.package_mirror (string) => local apt/yum/pip endpoint - var.skip_external_checks (bool) => set true in sealed envs; triggers local checks only - Use terraform providers with checksum and mirror options pinned in modules (avoid remote module download at apply time). - Strategy: vendor the terraform module (git subtree/submodule) into the release bundle and reference local path in CI-generated varfile. - State handling: recommend remote state via customer-managed S3 compatible store in the air-gapped network or local Postgres-backed Terraform Enterprise if available. Document fallback to local filesystem only for PoC. Upgrade plan (example for patch upgrade): - PREP: generate new bundle vX.Y, produce signed manifest and checksums. - STEP 0: create snapshot of current cluster state (etcd snapshot, db dump), store with a versioned name. - STEP 1: seed new images and charts into local registry (mirror). - STEP 2: deploy operator bundle as "canary" to a single namespace with replica overrides. Run smoke tests against canary. - STEP 3: if pass, rollout small percentage of traffic to new replicas (if using traffic routing). - STEP 4: monitor logs/metrics for 24–48 hours (or customer SLA window). - STEP 5: if stable, perform full rollout via helm/ops scripts. - ROLLBACK: use the pre-upgrade snapshot and recorded image digests to revert deploys. Keep operator bundle vprevious in local registry for quick reapply. Validation checks and smoke tests (automated): - API liveness: /health and /ready checks for each component. - End-to-end inference: small model run through a staging prompt set; verify response shape and latency threshold. - Data plane: embedding/rerank smoke queries if customer uses them. - Metrics and logs: check that metrics export is active and not failing due to network restrictions. - Storage validation: persistent volumes mount and read/write test. Troubleshooting common failure modes: - Images fail to pull: check registry_map, image tags, and that the local registry has the image digest matching manifest. - GPG/cosign mismatch: confirm signing keys and fingerprints. Provide explicit fingerprint in manifest to avoid trust confusion. - Terraform apply tries to fetch remote module: vendor modules locally; set TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE to a file that disables plugin discovery if necessary. - OS package missing dependency: ensure OS-packages snapshot includes kernel headers and basic build tools if wheels need native compilation. Minimal preflight checklist (run before apply): - [ ] Has customer provided a reachable bastion or transport channel? - [ ] Local registry present and reachable at var.offline_registry - [ ] checksums.txt matches the files on the transport medium - [ ] cosign/gpg verification passed for manifest and critical images - [ ] terraform module vendor folder present and referenced by TF_VARs - [ ] etcd snapshot storage destination reachable and has space (> 3x current size) Post-install notes and clean-up: - Remove transport credentials from bastion after import. - Archive bundle and checksums in customer-secure artifact repo. - Rotate any bootstrap keys used solely for bundle signing. Open TODOs / follow-ups: - Automate manifest generation (script in github repo) to include image digests and provider plugin checksums. - Add cosign transparency log step and include transparency log entry id in manifest. - Produce a smaller "quick-start" bundle for PoC installs under 15GB. Appendix: quick commands (examples) - Create image tar: docker save -o container-images.tar.gz $(cat image-list.txt) - Load and push to local registry: docker load -i container-images.tar.gz && docker tag local-registry/ && docker push local-registry/ - Verify GPG signature: gpg --verify manifest.yaml.sig manifest.yaml - Basic terraform offline apply: TF_DATA_DIR=/tmp/tfstate terraform apply -var-file=offline-vars.tfvars -parallelism=10 Notes to self: keep this doc concise and add an example manifest.yaml file and verify-bundle.sh script in the next iteration. Also coordinate with product-security to standardize signing key rotation guidance.
